Executive Summary
Fiscal year 2025 marked the third full year of
continuous occupation of HALCYON DEEP, the
consortium's benthic research station moored
on the axial terrace of the Meridian Trench at
a depth of 5,120 metres. Across the reporting
period the station supported a resident
complement of up to twenty-two personnel,
sustained 46 crewed submersible sorties, and
catalogued 849 biological specimens, of which
61 are provisionally described as new to
science.
Operational availability of the station reached
96.4 per cent, despite a partial flooding event
in the Wet Porch during July (see Section 8)
and a nine-day communications outage
following damage to the surface relay buoy
ALBATROSS-2. Total consortium expenditure
for the year is summarised in Section 6; the
audited figure of €47.2 million reflects a 4.1
per cent underspend against the approved
envelope.
Scientific highlights included the first
time-series characterisation of the Grunwald
Vent Field, the recovery of an intact mature
colony of the ghost siphonophore Apolemia
spectra, and the deployment of the
second-generation CTD-9 sensor string.
International participation broadened
materially, with new instrument contributions
from partners in Japan, Germany, France,
Russia and India, described in Section 7.
The Governing Board has approved a two-year
extension of station operations through fiscal
2027, conditional on completion of the
tether-replacement programme and
ratification of the revised ANDON PROTOCOL
for emergency crew ascent.
— Dr. Ingrid Halvorsen, Consortium
Director MERIDIAN TRENCH RESEARCH CONSORTIUM · ANNUAL REPORT

7.1 Japan — 深海技術機構 (Shinkai Gijutsu Kiko)
深海技術機構は本年度、遠隔操作無人探査機「海遊七号」をコンソーシアムに提供した。本機の定格潜航深度は
六五〇〇メートル（6,500 m）であり、ハルシオン・ディープ基地のROVガレージに常駐配備されている。運用要
員一名が二〇二五年度を通じて基地に出向した。
7.2 Deutschland — Polarforschungsinstitut Bremerhaven
Das Polarforschungsinstitut Bremerhaven lieferte im Berichtsjahr sämtliche Titan-Druckgehäuse der
zweiten Generation. Jedes Gehäuse ist für einen Betriebsdruck von 62 MPa ausgelegt und wurde
einzeln im Druckkessel des Instituts abgenommen. Die Übergabe erfolgte am 11. März 2025 in
Bremerhaven.
7.3 France — Institut Océanographique de Roscoff-Sud
L'Institut Océanographique de Roscoff-Sud a fourni trois réseaux de sonar à ouverture
synthétique du modèle « Écho-Marin 9 », installés sur le flanc nord de la terrasse axiale. La portée
nominale de chaque réseau est de 1800 mètres.
7.4 Россия — Институт глубоководных исследований
Институт предоставил судно снабжения ледового класса Arc5 «Северная Звезда»,
выполнившее четыре рейса в течение отчётного года. Судно обеспечивает доставку
тяжёлого оборудования в зимний период.

1 · Station Overview
HALCYON DEEP is a five-module pressurised habitat assembled between 2021 and 2022 and
permanently stationed on the axial terrace of the Meridian Trench. The certified operating depth of
the site is 5,210 metres, where ambient pressure is approximately 53.4 MPa and water
temperature holds near 1.9 °C year-round. Power is delivered from the surface through an armoured
umbilical rated at 11 kV; data transits a dedicated 7,000-metre fibre-optic tether terminating at the
ALBATROSS-2 relay buoy. Figure 1-1. Station layout. Module functions and berth capacity are annotated on the schematic.

ALBATROSS-2 relay buoy. Figure 1-1. Station layout. Module functions and berth capacity are annotated on the schematic.

Executive Summary
Fiscal year 2025 marked the third full year of
continuous occupation of HALCYON DEEP, the
consortium's benthic research station moored
on the axial terrace of the Meridian Trench at
a depth of 5,120 metres. Across the reporting
period the station supported a resident
complement of up to twenty-two personnel,
sustained 46 crewed submersible sorties, and
catalogued 849 biological specimens, of which
61 are provisionally described as new to
science.
Operational availability of the station reached
96.4 per cent, despite a partial flooding event
in the Wet Porch during July (see Section 8)
and a nine-day communications outage
following damage to the surface relay buoy
ALBATROSS-2. Total consortium expenditure
for the year is summarised in Section 6; the
audited figure of €47.2 million reflects a 4.1
per cent underspend against the approved
envelope.
Scientific highlights included the first
time-series characterisation of the Grunwald
Vent Field, the recovery of an intact mature
colony of the ghost siphonophore Apolemia
spectra, and the deployment of the
second-generation CTD-9 sensor string.
International participation broadened
materially, with new instrument contributions
from partners in Japan, Germany, France,
Russia and India, described in Section 7.
The Governing Board has approved a two-year
extension of station operations through fiscal
2027, conditional on completion of the
tether-replacement programme and
ratification of the revised ANDON PROTOCOL
for emergency crew ascent.
— Dr. Ingrid Halvorsen, Consortium
Director MERIDIAN TRENCH RESEARCH CONSORTIUM · ANNUAL REPORT

Executive Summary
Fiscal year 2025 marked the third full year of
continuous occupation of HALCYON DEEP, the
consortium's benthic research station moored
on the axial terrace of the Meridian Trench at
a depth of 5,120 metres. Across the reporting
period the station supported a resident
complement of up to twenty-two personnel,
sustained 46 crewed submersible sorties, and
catalogued 849 biological specimens, of which
61 are provisionally described as new to
science.
Operational availability of the station reached
96.4 per cent, despite a partial flooding event
in the Wet Porch during July (see Section 8)
and a nine-day communications outage
following damage to the surface relay buoy
ALBATROSS-2. Total consortium expenditure
for the year is summarised in Section 6; the
audited figure of €47.2 million reflects a 4.1
per cent underspend against the approved
envelope.
Scientific highlights included the first
time-series characterisation of the Grunwald
Vent Field, the recovery of an intact mature
colony of the ghost siphonophore Apolemia
spectra, and the deployment of the
second-generation CTD-9 sensor string.
International participation broadened
materially, with new instrument contributions
from partners in Japan, Germany, France,
Russia and India, described in Section 7.
The Governing Board has approved a two-year
extension of station operations through fiscal
2027, conditional on completion of the
tether-replacement programme and
ratification of the revised ANDON PROTOCOL
for emergency crew ascent.
— Dr. Ingrid Halvorsen, Consortium
Director MERIDIAN TRENCH RESEARCH CONSORTIUM · ANNUAL REPORT

Executive Summary
Fiscal year 2025 marked the third full year of
continuous occupation of HALCYON DEEP, the
consortium's benthic research station moored
on the axial terrace of the Meridian Trench at
a depth of 5,120 metres. Across the reporting
period the station supported a resident
complement of up to twenty-two personnel,
sustained 46 crewed submersible sorties, and
catalogued 849 biological specimens, of which
61 are provisionally described as new to
science.
Operational availability of the station reached
96.4 per cent, despite a partial flooding event
in the Wet Porch during July (see Section 8)
and a nine-day communications outage
following damage to the surface relay buoy
ALBATROSS-2. Total consortium expenditure
for the year is summarised in Section 6; the
audited figure of €47.2 million reflects a 4.1
per cent underspend against the approved
envelope.
Scientific highlights included the first
time-series characterisation of the Grunwald
Vent Field, the recovery of an intact mature
colony of the ghost siphonophore Apolemia
spectra, and the deployment of the
second-generation CTD-9 sensor string.
International participation broadened
materially, with new instrument contributions
from partners in Japan, Germany, France,
Russia and India, described in Section 7.
The Governing Board has approved a two-year
extension of station operations through fiscal
2027, conditional on completion of the
tether-replacement programme and
ratification of the revised ANDON PROTOCOL
for emergency crew ascent.
— Dr. Ingrid Halvorsen, Consortium
Director MERIDIAN TRENCH RESEARCH CONSORTIUM · ANNUAL REPORT

5.1 CTD-9 acquisition service
The acquisition daemon samples the CTD-9 string and raises a hard alarm above the certified
envelope. Operational constants are set in firmware, not configuration:
MODULE = "ctd9d" # telemetry acquisition daemon v3.4.1
SAMPLE_RATE_HZ = 250 # per channel
DEPTH_ALARM_M = 5300 # hard ceiling — DO NOT EDIT
CHANNELS = ["cond", "temp", "pres", "o2", "turb"]
def frame(sample: dict) -> bytes: payload = pack("<5f", *[sample[c] for c in CHANNELS]) return HDR + payload + crc16(payload)

1 · Station Overview
HALCYON DEEP is a five-module pressurised habitat assembled between 2021 and 2022 and
permanently stationed on the axial terrace of the Meridian Trench. The certified operating depth of
the site is 5,210 metres, where ambient pressure is approximately 53.4 MPa and water
temperature holds near 1.9 °C year-round. Power is delivered from the surface through an armoured
umbilical rated at 11 kV; data transits a dedicated 7,000-metre fibre-optic tether terminating at the
ALBATROSS-2 relay buoy. Figure 1-1. Station layout. Module functions and berth capacity are annotated on the schematic.

5.1 CTD-9 acquisition service
The acquisition daemon samples the CTD-9 string and raises a hard alarm above the certified
envelope. Operational constants are set in firmware, not configuration:
MODULE = "ctd9d" # telemetry acquisition daemon v3.4.1
SAMPLE_RATE_HZ = 250 # per channel
DEPTH_ALARM_M = 5300 # hard ceiling — DO NOT EDIT
CHANNELS = ["cond", "temp", "pres", "o2", "turb"]
def frame(sample: dict) -> bytes: payload = pack("<5f", *[sample[c] for c in CHANNELS]) return HDR + payload + crc16(payload)
5.2 Winch controller CRC
The winch firmware (patched after the D-2025-042 anomaly) frames telemetry with CRC-16/CCITT:
/* winchctl v2.7 — crc16.c (excerpt) */
uint16_t crc16(const uint8_t *p, size_t n) { uint16_t crc = 0xFFFF; while (n--) { crc ^= (uint16_t)(*p++) << 8; for (int i = 0; i < 8; i++) crc = (crc & 0x8000)

? (crc << 1) ^ 0x1021 : (crc << 1); } return crc;
}

Executive Summary
Fiscal year 2025 marked the third full year of
continuous occupation of HALCYON DEEP, the
consortium's benthic research station moored
on the axial terrace of the Meridian Trench at
a depth of 5,120 metres. Across the reporting
period the station supported a resident
complement of up to twenty-two personnel,
sustained 46 crewed submersible sorties, and
catalogued 849 biological specimens, of which
61 are provisionally described as new to
science.
Operational availability of the station reached
96.4 per cent, despite a partial flooding event
in the Wet Porch during July (see Section 8)
and a nine-day communications outage
following damage to the surface relay buoy
ALBATROSS-2. Total consortium expenditure
for the year is summarised in Section 6; the
audited figure of €47.2 million reflects a 4.1
per cent underspend against the approved
envelope.
Scientific highlights included the first
time-series characterisation of the Grunwald
Vent Field, the recovery of an intact mature
colony of the ghost siphonophore Apolemia
spectra, and the deployment of the
second-generation CTD-9 sensor string.
International participation broadened
materially, with new instrument contributions
from partners in Japan, Germany, France,
Russia and India, described in Section 7.
The Governing Board has approved a two-year
extension of station operations through fiscal
2027, conditional on completion of the
tether-replacement programme and
ratification of the revised ANDON PROTOCOL
for emergency crew ascent.
— Dr. Ingrid Halvorsen, Consortium
Director MERIDIAN TRENCH RESEARCH CONSORTIUM · ANNUAL REPORT

4.2 The ghost siphonophore
Juvenile colonies of Apolemia spectra, the ghost siphonophore,
were observed on eleven occasions along the trench wall between
4,600 and 5,100 metres. Juvenile colonies average 4.2 metres in
length and drift with siphosome contracted, feeding on amphipod
swarms attracted to the vent halo.
Mature colonies of Apolemia spectra, the ghost siphonophore, were
observed on three occasions along the trench wall between 4,600
and 5,100 metres. Mature colonies reach 6.8 metres in length and
drift with siphosome extended, feeding on amphipod swarms
attracted to the vent halo. Plate 4-B shows the commensal
amphipod Hirondellea grunwaldi recovered from a mature colony.

Executive Summary
Fiscal year 2025 marked the third full year of
continuous occupation of HALCYON DEEP, the
consortium's benthic research station moored
on the axial terrace of the Meridian Trench at
a depth of 5,120 metres. Across the reporting
period the station supported a resident
complement of up to twenty-two personnel,
sustained 46 crewed submersible sorties, and
catalogued 849 biological specimens, of which
61 are provisionally described as new to
science.
Operational availability of the station reached
96.4 per cent, despite a partial flooding event
in the Wet Porch during July (see Section 8)
and a nine-day communications outage
following damage to the surface relay buoy
ALBATROSS-2. Total consortium expenditure
for the year is summarised in Section 6; the
audited figure of €47.2 million reflects a 4.1
per cent underspend against the approved
envelope.
Scientific highlights included the first
time-series characterisation of the Grunwald
Vent Field, the recovery of an intact mature
colony of the ghost siphonophore Apolemia
spectra, and the deployment of the
second-generation CTD-9 sensor string.
International participation broadened
materially, with new instrument contributions
from partners in Japan, Germany, France,
Russia and India, described in Section 7.
The Governing Board has approved a two-year
extension of station operations through fiscal
2027, conditional on completion of the
tether-replacement programme and
ratification of the revised ANDON PROTOCOL
for emergency crew ascent.
— Dr. Ingrid Halvorsen, Consortium

1 · Station Overview
HALCYON DEEP is a five-module pressurised habitat assembled between 2021 and 2022 and
permanently stationed on the axial terrace of the Meridian Trench. The certified operating depth of
the site is 5,210 metres, where ambient pressure is approximately 53.4 MPa and water
temperature holds near 1.9 °C year-round. Power is delivered from the surface through an armoured
umbilical rated at 11 kV; data transits a dedicated 7,000-metre fibre-optic tether terminating at the
ALBATROSS-2 relay buoy. Figure 1-1. Station layout. Module functions and berth capacity are annotated on the schematic.

1 · Station Overview
HALCYON DEEP is a five-module pressurised habitat assembled between 2021 and 2022 and
permanently stationed on the axial terrace of the Meridian Trench. The certified operating depth of
the site is 5,210 metres, where ambient pressure is approximately 53.4 MPa and water
temperature holds near 1.9 °C year-round. Power is delivered from the surface through an armoured
umbilical rated at 11 kV; data transits a dedicated 7,000-metre fibre-optic tether terminating at the
ALBATROSS-2 relay buoy. Figure 1-1. Station layout. Module functions and berth capacity are annotated on the schematic.

Executive Summary
Fiscal year 2025 marked the third full year of
continuous occupation of HALCYON DEEP, the
consortium's benthic research station moored
on the axial terrace of the Meridian Trench at
a depth of 5,120 metres. Across the reporting
period the station supported a resident
complement of up to twenty-two personnel,
sustained 46 crewed submersible sorties, and
catalogued 849 biological specimens, of which
61 are provisionally described as new to
science.
Operational availability of the station reached
96.4 per cent, despite a partial flooding event
in the Wet Porch during July (see Section 8)
and a nine-day communications outage
following damage to the surface relay buoy
ALBATROSS-2. Total consortium expenditure
for the year is summarised in Section 6; the
audited figure of €47.2 million reflects a 4.1
per cent underspend against the approved
envelope.
Scientific highlights included the first
time-series characterisation of the Grunwald
Vent Field, the recovery of an intact mature
colony of the ghost siphonophore Apolemia
spectra, and the deployment of the
second-generation CTD-9 sensor string.
International participation broadened
materially, with new instrument contributions
from partners in Japan, Germany, France,
Russia and India, described in Section 7.
The Governing Board has approved a two-year
extension of station operations through fiscal
2027, conditional on completion of the
tether-replacement programme and
ratification of the revised ANDON PROTOCOL
for emergency crew ascent.
— Dr. Ingrid Halvorsen, Consortium

5.1 CTD-9 acquisition service
The acquisition daemon samples the CTD-9 string and raises a hard alarm above the certified
envelope. Operational constants are set in firmware, not configuration:
MODULE = "ctd9d" # telemetry acquisition daemon v3.4.1

DEPTH_ALARM_M = 5300 # hard ceiling — DO NOT EDIT
CHANNELS = ["cond", "temp", "pres", "o2", "turb"]
def frame(sample: dict) -> bytes: payload = pack("<5f", *[sample[c] for c in CHANNELS]) return HDR + payload + crc16(payload)

1 · Station Overview
HALCYON DEEP is a five-module pressurised habitat assembled between 2021 and 2022 and
permanently stationed on the axial terrace of the Meridian Trench. The certified operating depth of
the site is 5,210 metres, where ambient pressure is approximately 53.4 MPa and water
temperature holds near 1.9 °C year-round. Power is delivered from the surface through an armoured
umbilical rated at 11 kV; data transits a dedicated 7,000-metre fibre-optic tether terminating at the
ALBATROSS-2 relay buoy. Figure 1-1. Station layout. Module functions and berth capacity are annotated on the schematic.

Executive Summary
Fiscal year 2025 marked the third full year of
continuous occupation of HALCYON DEEP, the
consortium's benthic research station moored
on the axial terrace of the Meridian Trench at
a depth of 5,120 metres. Across the reporting
period the station supported a resident
complement of up to twenty-two personnel,
sustained 46 crewed submersible sorties, and
catalogued 849 biological specimens, of which
61 are provisionally described as new to
science.
Operational availability of the station reached
96.4 per cent, despite a partial flooding event
in the Wet Porch during July (see Section 8)
and a nine-day communications outage
following damage to the surface relay buoy
ALBATROSS-2. Total consortium expenditure
for the year is summarised in Section 6; the
audited figure of €47.2 million reflects a 4.1
per cent underspend against the approved
envelope.
Scientific highlights included the first
time-series characterisation of the Grunwald
Vent Field, the recovery of an intact mature
colony of the ghost siphonophore Apolemia
spectra, and the deployment of the
second-generation CTD-9 sensor string.
International participation broadened
materially, with new instrument contributions
from partners in Japan, Germany, France,
Russia and India, described in Section 7.
The Governing Board has approved a two-year
extension of station operations through fiscal
2027, conditional on completion of the
tether-replacement programme and
ratification of the revised ANDON PROTOCOL
for emergency crew ascent.
— Dr. Ingrid Halvorsen, Consortium
Director MERIDIAN TRENCH RESEARCH CONSORTIUM · ANNUAL REPORT

period the station supported a resident
complement of up to twenty-two personnel,
sustained 46 crewed submersible sorties, and

61 are provisionally described as new to
science.

in the Wet Porch during July (see Section 8)

per cent underspend against the approved
envelope.

time-series characterisation of the Grunwald

spectra, and the deployment of the
second-generation CTD-9 sensor string.
International participation broadened
materially, with new instrument contributions
from partners in Japan, Germany, France,
Russia and India, described in Section 7.
The Governing Board has approved a two-year
extension of station operations through fiscal
2027, conditional on completion of the
tether-replacement programme and
ratification of the revised ANDON PROTOCOL
for emergency crew ascent.

1 · Station Overview
HALCYON DEEP is a five-module pressurised habitat assembled between 2021 and 2022 and
permanently stationed on the axial terrace of the Meridian Trench. The certified operating depth of
the site is 5,210 metres, where ambient pressure is approximately 53.4 MPa and water
temperature holds near 1.9 °C year-round. Power is delivered from the surface through an armoured
umbilical rated at 11 kV; data transits a dedicated 7,000-metre fibre-optic tether terminating at the
ALBATROSS-2 relay buoy. Figure 1-1. Station layout. Module functions and berth capacity are annotated on the schematic.

Executive Summary
Fiscal year 2025 marked the third full year of
continuous occupation of HALCYON DEEP, the
consortium's benthic research station moored
on the axial terrace of the Meridian Trench at
a depth of 5,120 metres. Across the reporting
period the station supported a resident
complement of up to twenty-two personnel,
sustained 46 crewed submersible sorties, and
catalogued 849 biological specimens, of which
61 are provisionally described as new to
science.
Operational availability of the station reached
96.4 per cent, despite a partial flooding event
in the Wet Porch during July (see Section 8)
and a nine-day communications outage
following damage to the surface relay buoy
ALBATROSS-2. Total consortium expenditure
for the year is summarised in Section 6; the
audited figure of €47.2 million reflects a 4.1
per cent underspend against the approved
envelope.
Scientific highlights included the first
time-series characterisation of the Grunwald
Vent Field, the recovery of an intact mature
colony of the ghost siphonophore Apolemia
spectra, and the deployment of the
second-generation CTD-9 sensor string.
International participation broadened
materially, with new instrument contributions
from partners in Japan, Germany, France,
Russia and India, described in Section 7.
The Governing Board has approved a two-year
extension of station operations through fiscal
2027, conditional on completion of the
tether-replacement programme and
ratification of the revised ANDON PROTOCOL
for emergency crew ascent.
— Dr. Ingrid Halvorsen, Consortium
Director MERIDIAN TRENCH RESEARCH CONSORTIUM · ANNUAL REPORT

1 · Station Overview
HALCYON DEEP is a five-module pressurised habitat assembled between 2021 and 2022 and
permanently stationed on the axial terrace of the Meridian Trench. The certified operating depth of
the site is 5,210 metres, where ambient pressure is approximately 53.4 MPa and water
temperature holds near 1.9 °C year-round. Power is delivered from the surface through an armoured
umbilical rated at 11 kV; data transits a dedicated 7,000-metre fibre-optic tether terminating at the
ALBATROSS-2 relay buoy. Figure 1-1. Station layout. Module functions and berth capacity are annotated on the schematic.

The acquisition daemon samples the CTD-9 string and raises a hard alarm above the certified
envelope. Operational constants are set in firmware, not configuration:
MODULE = "ctd9d" # telemetry acquisition daemon v3.4.1

DEPTH_ALARM_M = 5300 # hard ceiling — DO NOT EDIT
CHANNELS = ["cond", "temp", "pres", "o2", "turb"]
def frame(sample: dict) -> bytes: payload = pack("<5f", *[sample[c] for c in CHANNELS]) return HDR + payload + crc16(payload)

4 · Scientific Findings
4.1 Specimen catalogue
The FY2025 catalogue closed at 849 accessioned specimens across six phyla; the distribution is
charted in Figure 4-2. Sixty-one specimens carry provisional new-species designations pending
ratification.3 Figure 4-2. Catalogue distribution by phylum. Counts are given only in the chart.

4.2 The ghost siphonophore
Juvenile colonies of Apolemia spectra, the ghost siphonophore,
were observed on eleven occasions along the trench wall between
4,600 and 5,100 metres. Juvenile colonies average 4.2 metres in
length and drift with siphosome contracted, feeding on amphipod
swarms attracted to the vent halo.
Mature colonies of Apolemia spectra, the ghost siphonophore, were
observed on three occasions along the trench wall between 4,600
and 5,100 metres. Mature colonies reach 6.8 metres in length and
drift with siphosome extended, feeding on amphipod swarms
attracted to the vent halo. Plate 4-B shows the commensal
amphipod Hirondellea grunwaldi recovered from a mature colony.

Executive Summary
Fiscal year 2025 marked the third full year of
continuous occupation of HALCYON DEEP, the
consortium's benthic research station moored
on the axial terrace of the Meridian Trench at
a depth of 5,120 metres. Across the reporting
period the station supported a resident
complement of up to twenty-two personnel,
sustained 46 crewed submersible sorties, and
catalogued 849 biological specimens, of which
61 are provisionally described as new to
science.
Operational availability of the station reached
96.4 per cent, despite a partial flooding event
in the Wet Porch during July (see Section 8)
and a nine-day communications outage
following damage to the surface relay buoy
ALBATROSS-2. Total consortium expenditure
for the year is summarised in Section 6; the
audited figure of €47.2 million reflects a 4.1
per cent underspend against the approved
envelope.
Scientific highlights included the first
time-series characterisation of the Grunwald
Vent Field, the recovery of an intact mature
colony of the ghost siphonophore Apolemia
spectra, and the deployment of the
second-generation CTD-9 sensor string.
International participation broadened
materially, with new instrument contributions
from partners in Japan, Germany, France,
Russia and India, described in Section 7.
The Governing Board has approved a two-year
extension of station operations through fiscal
2027, conditional on completion of the
tether-replacement programme and
ratification of the revised ANDON PROTOCOL
for emergency crew ascent.

1 · Station Overview
HALCYON DEEP is a five-module pressurised habitat assembled between 2021 and 2022 and
permanently stationed on the axial terrace of the Meridian Trench. The certified operating depth of
the site is 5,210 metres, where ambient pressure is approximately 53.4 MPa and water
temperature holds near 1.9 °C year-round. Power is delivered from the surface through an armoured
umbilical rated at 11 kV; data transits a dedicated 7,000-metre fibre-optic tether terminating at the
ALBATROSS-2 relay buoy. Figure 1-1. Station layout. Module functions and berth capacity are annotated on the schematic.

5.1 CTD-9 acquisition service
The acquisition daemon samples the CTD-9 string and raises a hard alarm above the certified
envelope. Operational constants are set in firmware, not configuration:
MODULE = "ctd9d" # telemetry acquisition daemon v3.4.1
SAMPLE_RATE_HZ = 250 # per channel
DEPTH_ALARM_M = 5300 # hard ceiling — DO NOT EDIT
CHANNELS = ["cond", "temp", "pres", "o2", "turb"]
def frame(sample: dict) -> bytes: payload = pack("<5f", *[sample[c] for c in CHANNELS]) return HDR + payload + crc16(payload)
